title: Preah Vihear Temple
summary: Preah Vihear is a Khmer Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, set on the edge of a plateau in the Dangrek range on the Cambodia–Thailand border. UNESCO dates the complex to the first half of the 11th century, with a hermitage there from the 9th century. It was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2008.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO dates the temple to the first half of the 11th century and traces the site to a 9th-century hermitage; WorldAtlas says building continued over centuries, mostly under Suryavarman I (1006-1050) and Suryavarman II (1113-1150). World Heritage inscription was in 2008.

as_recorded.value: first half of the 11th century AD

when.display: First half of the 11th century CE (inscribed UNESCO 2008)

importance.justification: UNESCO World Heritage Khmer temple whose ownership was disputed between Cambodia and Thailand.

reviewer_note: Pin is UNESCO's listed coordinate (N14 23 27.028 E104 40 49.17) converted to decimal. Construction dates vary: UNESCO says first half of 11th c.; WorldAtlas says begun 9th c., main phases 1006-1050 and 1113-1150. Second source is a general web publisher.
